rated_messages.input_message: Take a deep breath. Focus on today and the things you have accomplished. How many urges have you let pass? Give yourself some credit!
See what it is like to let the urge pass. You can have an urge and choose not to smoke.
You spent a long time training your brain to want a cig. Now you're retraining your brain, and it's natural that this might take time.
What can you do right now to break the automatic habit of smoking when you are here? Pause. Close your eyes. And take 10 slow breaths.
One way to combat any urges is to keep your mouth busy - some people find that chewing sugar free gum, mints, or even a pen can be a good alternative.
Have confidence in knowing that you can have this urge, choose not to smoke, be okay, and choose to do things that matter most to you.

Reduce your stress by using your next break to list four things that have gone well so far today. It might feel like a bit of effort, but doing this will help your mind to refocus, and help you to feel calmer.
Instead of smoking, think of 3 things from today that you are grateful for. These can be anything, even small things! Now ask yourself, why are you grateful for these things?
Instead of smoking, use the next two minutes to pay close attention to your senses. Notice what you see, hear, feel, taste, and smell. Urges are just one part of your experience.
It's normal to have some doubts during a quit attempt. Keep your quit reasons on hand to remind yourself if ever you feel uncertain or undecided.
